newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks close up slightly on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks close up slightly on selective buying.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange closed up slightly Thursday in improved trade dominated by selective buying by local investors, brokers said.

Analysts said major investors were waiting on the sidelines until the official announcement of Peru's 1996 gross domestic product figure, meaning that prices were expected to close the week little changed.
The General Index edged up 0.37 percent to 1,529.25 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index also gained 0.65 percent to 2,208.94 points.
In a total of 1,406 trades, volume was estimated at 24 million soles ($9.1 million), brokers said.

"Many are waiting for the official 1996 GDP figure before taking an initiative so they are only investing into shares from the public services and mining sectors," said Victor Heredia of the Fortuna brokerage.
Among leading stocks, brewers Backus y Johnston rose 1.37 percent to 2.22 soles on 490,464 shares and benchmark telephone company Telefonica de Peru rose 0.71 percent to 5.68 soles on 697,780 shares.
Despite recent caution brokers insisted that medium and long term prospects for the exchange were positive.
"The long term economic prospects for Peru are a good incentive for investors to enter the market to trade with more enthusiasm," said Mirko Ibanez of the Intercapital brokerage.
